# Neuroendocrine Tumor 177Lutetium-Dotatate Therapy

**Authors:** Robert B. Killeen, Dawood Tafti

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) represent a rare and heterogeneous group of malignancies with variable clinical behavior, most commonly arising in the gastrointestinal tract and pancreas. While early-stage disease can be managed effectively with surgery, advanced or unresectable NETs often require systemic therapies. This activity will review peptide receptor radioligand therapy (PRRT) with Lutetium-177 (177Lu)-dotatate, which has emerged as a major therapeutic advancement, particularly in well-differentiated, somatostatin receptor-positive tumors. Clinical trials, including the landmark NETTER-1 study, have demonstrated significant improvements in progression-free survival, quality of life, and symptom control with 177Lu-dotatate compared with standard therapy. Participants will gain an understanding that despite risks such as hematologic toxicity, renal impairment, and rare myeloid neoplasms, 177Lu-dotatate remains an effective and FDA-approved option for patients who progress on somatostatin analogs.
